articles.title: Reading SMD resistor codes without guessing
articles.excerpt: A 0603 resistor falls off the tweezers and lands face up, and the marking is 472. That is either 4.7k or 47k depending on which digit your eye decides is The codes are arithmetic, except when they are…
articles.body: A 0603 resistor falls off the tweezers and lands face up, and the marking is 472 . That is either 4.7k or 47k depending on which digit your eye decides is the multiplier. Two minutes later you have measured the wrong one and the divider is off by a factor of ten. The codes are arithmetic, except when they are not. Three systems cover almost everything on a hobby bench, and each fails in its own way. The three digit code Three digits: the first two are the value, the third is how many zeros to add. 472 is 47 followed by two zeros: 4,700 ohms, 4.7k. 103 is 10 followed by three zeros: 10,000 ohms, 10k. 221 is 220 ohms. 100 is 10 ohms, because zero zeros is a real answer. This is the most common marking on cheap parts, and it is usually a 5 percent part.

articles.title: How 3D Vision Lets Painting Robots Program Themselves
articles.excerpt: Painting a part with a robot used to start with a long teaching session. A programmer would guide the arm through each pass, save every waypoint, and then adjust the spray by trial and error. That wor…
articles.body: Painting a part with a robot used to start with a long teaching session. A programmer would guide the arm through each pass, save every waypoint, and then adjust the spray by trial and error. That works for a line that makes the same product for years, but it breaks down when a factory handles many part types in small batches. 3D vision is changing that, because it lets painting robots program themselves. Step 1: See the part A depth camera or laser scanner captures the workpiece as a point cloud, usually in a few seconds. The system does not need a CAD file or a fixture with a known position. It simply measures what is actually in front of it, including parts that sit slightly rotated, warped, or hung at an odd angle on the conveyor.

articles.title: Supabase confirmation or reset email opens localhost:3000? Here's the fix
articles.excerpt: A user signs up for your live app, clicks the confirmation link, and the browser says: localhost:3000 refused to connect Password reset emails do the same. Nothing is wrong with your deploy. Supabase…
articles.body: A user signs up for your live app, clicks the confirmation link, and the browser says: localhost:3000 refused to connect Password reset emails do the same. Nothing is wrong with your deploy. Supabase builds email links from the project's Site URL , and a new project starts with that set to http://localhost:3000 . Set the Site URL to your live domain, add every address you redirect to under Redirect URLs , and pass a redirect address from the app that is on that list. I see this a lot in apps built with Lovable, Bolt and Replit on Supabase, usually right after the first real users arrive. Why it happens The Site URL is still the default. Every confirmation and reset link falls back to it, so they all point at localhost:3000 . The redirect address isn't allowed.

articles.title: Running a Python or LangGraph Agent as a Flisk Worker, With Dependencies Declared
articles.excerpt: Not every agent answers HTTP requests. Some work through a queue: they pick up a task, call a model, write a result, and wait for the next one. Flisk's worker resource type fits that shape. The docs d…
articles.body: Not every agent answers HTTP requests. Some work through a queue: they pick up a task, call a model, write a result, and wait for the next one. Flisk's worker resource type fits that shape. The docs describe a Python or LangGraph agent running as a worker, with Postgres and NATS declared as dependencies. Scaffold the worker flisk resource research-agent --type worker --stack shop --yes Then declare what the worker needs in its service.json : { "name" : "research-agent" , "appType" : "worker" , "stack" : "shop" , "dependsOn" : [ "postgres" , "nats" ], "env" : { "DATABASE_URL" : "@ref(postgres.DATABASE_URL)" , "NATS_URL" : "@ref(nats.NATS_URL)" } } The dependsOn list sets the start order.

articles.title: Flisk as a Control Plane: Let Your Coding Assistant Run the Whole Local Stack
articles.excerpt: The mcp resource puts an agent's tools inside your stack. The flisk mcp command does the reverse: it lets an assistant control the stack. Run it over stdio, and a coding assistant can check the machin…
articles.body: The mcp resource puts an agent's tools inside your stack. The flisk mcp command does the reverse: it lets an assistant control the stack. Run it over stdio, and a coding assistant can check the machine, start services, read their status, and read bounded logs. Connect it The Flisk docs give the same entry for the MCP clients they name, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex: { "mcpServers" : { "flisk" : { "command" : "flisk" , "args" : [ "mcp" ] } } } The server runs from the project folder, so it finds the project's configuration. Set the working directory in your client, or the assistant will be looking in the wrong place. What it can do The docs list four jobs: doctor diagnoses the container runtime and port conflicts. up and down start and stop services.
